full_judgment:
6. Respondent appellant No.4, Commissioner of Revenue, Khulna Area, Khulna, contested the cases by filing written statements controverting the material statements made in the cases. His case, in short, is that the cases filed by the respondents are barred by limitation. The further case of this appellant is that the respondents were appointed on 29.12.1986 as Lower Division Assistants under the Tax Circle of Khulna. The letter dated 15.10.1987 reveals that the Second Secretary (Administration), Md. Mosarraf Hossain, who is now under suspension, in order to illegally gain financial benefit, appointed the respondents along with others on the basis of false nomination of the Ministry of Establishment. A 3-member inquiry committee was formed headed by Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, Farid Ahmed along with two other Members and the respondents appeared before the Inquiry Board with their relevant papers and they made out their case both orally and in writing. As the allegations brought against the respondents were proved beyond doubt, they were dismissed from service as per Rule 4 (3)(d) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules,1985 and as such, the respondents are not entitled to get any relief. 

 10. Mr. Biswajit Debnath, learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the appellants of all the civil appeals, submits that the respondents were dismissed from service on 31.01.1988 and that they filed departmental appeals on 24.11.2008 beyond the statutory period of limitation as per Rule 18 of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules,1985 and the cases before the Administrative Tribunal were filed on 28.04.2009 after long lapse of almost 22 years and as such, the Administrative Tribunal committed error of law in holding that the cases were filed within the statutory period of limitation and that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal without considering the question of limitation dis-missed the appeals and as such, the impugned decision should be set aside. 

 13. Leave was granted in all the appeals to consider whether the cases filed by the respondents before the Administrative Tribunal were barred by limitation. 

 14. The Administrative Tribunal came to a finding that the cases filed by the respondents were within the period of limitation. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal, however, did not give any finding as to the question of limitation. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal found that as the respondents were appointed by the appointing authority, the respondents had no hand to manipulate the order of appointment and as such, they had acquired a vested right as being appointed as Lower Division Assistants. 

 15. The fate of the appeals hinges on the question of limitation. 

 16. In order to resolve the question of limitation, it would be pertinent to quote section 4 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980: 

 18. Admittedly, the respondents were dismissed from service on 31.01.1988 and that they filed the departmental appeals on 24.11.2008 and according to them, they came to know about the dismissal order on 04.11.2008. The Administrative Tribunal came to a finding that as the appeals of the respondents were not disposed of within 2 (two) months, the respondents filed the cases within the statutory period of limitation, that is, within 6 (six) months from the expiry of 2 (two) months of filing of the appeals. 

 20. In this connection, reliance may be placed on the case of Md. Nazimuddin Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, (2012) 17 BLC (AD) 10 where it has been held that according to the 2nd proviso, if an appeal or application for review is filed and if the higher administrative authority does not take any decision on such appeal or application for review within two months then such appeal or application for review shall be deemed to have been disallowed after expiry of that period. If the word "disallowed" as mentioned in the 2nd proviso is construed as a decision or order by higher authority as contemplated under the 3rd proviso then there exists a harmonious construction between the 2nd and the 3rd provisos and in fact, the legislature intended as such. In that event, the period of computation of limitation of six months as contained in the 3rd proviso will start running from the date when an appeal or application for review shall be deemed to have been disallowed as contemplated under the 2nd proviso. 

 21. The principle expounded in the case referred to above applies to the facts and circumstances of the present case as the respondents were admittedly dismissed from service on 31.01.1988. The departmental appeals should have been filed by the respondents within 6 (six) months from 31.01.1988 but the respondents filed the departmental appeals on 24.11.2008 and as such, there is no scope for computing the period of limitation from 24.11.2008. 

 22. The finding of the Administrative Tribunal in respect of limitation in filing the cases is wrong and contrary to the provision of the 2nd proviso to section 4(2) of the Act. 

 23. Admittedly, the respondents were dismissed from service following the procedures as contained in Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 and as such the Administrative Appellate Tribunal erred in law in dismissing the appeals, which, however, did not consider the question of limitation at all.
